youtube.title: The year gets thousands of days
youtube.caption:
A year holds about 1,460 days at a six hour day, over 6,000 at the end, with a sunrise every 84 minutes.

Part 6 of 8 of "What If Earth Spun Faster and Couldn't Stop?" — the full video is on this channel.

Sources
1. At a day of 1 hour 24 minutes a year holds about 6,200 days (365.25 days × 23.93 h ÷ 1.41 h). (our calculation; the arithmetic is shown in the film)
2. At a 6 h day a year holds 1,461 days (365.25 days × 24 h ÷ 6 h). (our calculation; the arithmetic is shown in the film)
3. At 45° north your speed is 71% of the equator's and the outward push on you is 50%. (our calculation; the arithmetic is shown in the film)
4. Your weight as a share of what it would be on a non-spinning Earth: 99.7% today, 98.6% at a 12 h day, 94.5% at 6 h, 78.0% at 3 h, 50.4% at 2 h and 11.9% at 1.5 h. A 70 kg person weighs 69 kg at 12 h and 55 kg at 3 h. (our calculation; the arithmetic is shown in the film)
5. The faster Earth spins, the higher the sea wants to stand at the equator compared with the poles: 33 km higher at a 12 h day, and far more as the day gets shorter. (our calculation; the arithmetic is shown in the film)

Narration: synthetic voice (AI). Thumbnail illustration made with AI. Animation: code-rendered, no stock footage. Every number is checked against the sources.

Possibility Lab: Impossible questions, honest assumptions, real calculations.
